findings.title: Force unwrap of Double(text) crashes on invalid pasted input
findings.explanation: The comment states the input is arbitrary pasted text and that invalid amounts must produce an error, but `Double(text)!` force-unwraps the optional. For any non-numeric text (e.g. "abc", "1,234.56" with a locale comma, "12 USD", empty string) `Double(text)` returns nil and the force unwrap triggers a runtime trap, crashing the app instead of reporting an error. Additionally, Double(text) does not trim whitespace, so a pasted amount like " 12.50 " or "12.50\n" also returns nil and crashes.
findings.recommendation: Do not force unwrap. Either change the signature to `func parseAmount(_ text: String) throws -> Double` and throw a descriptive error, or return a Result/optional and have the caller handle failure. Trim whitespace and reject non-numeric input explicitly.
findings.suggested_test: Call parseAmount("abc") and assert it returns nil / throws a defined error rather than trapping; call parseAmount(" 12.50 ") and assert the parsed value is 12.50.

findings.title: Return type cannot express the error required by the documented contract
findings.evidence:
func parseAmount(_ text: String) -> Double {
    // Input is arbitrary pasted text; invalid amounts must produce an error.
findings.explanation: The signature returns a non-optional Double and the function is not `throws`, so it has no way to signal the error its own comment promises. This forces the implementation to use a force unwrap, which is the root cause of the crash. The API contract is inconsistent with its documented behavior.
findings.recommendation: Align the API with the contract: `func parseAmount(_ text: String) throws -> Double` (or return `Double?`/Result) so callers must handle invalid input.
findings.suggested_test: Compile-time check that the function can fail, plus a unit test asserting a thrown error for "not-a-number".

findings.title: No test coverage for the parsing helper
findings.explanation: The only parsing logic in the file has no accompanying tests in the reviewed source, so the crash-on-invalid-input behavior and the whitespace/locale edge cases are unguarded against regressions.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests covering valid integers, decimals, negative values, whitespace-padded input, empty string, and non-numeric strings.
findings.suggested_test: Table-driven XCTest: ("12", 12.0), ("12.5", 12.5), ("-3.2", -3.2), (" 7 ", 7.0), and invalid inputs "abc", "", "12,5" assert failure rather than a trap.
